one_line_for_the_editor: This is the second paper in the Precompute×$E$ cell, and it breaks the sentence printed in OUTLOOK §5.1 ("2026-08 기준으로도 그 열은 그 한 편뿐이다"). It also inverts Letta STC on almost every accounting axis: it PRINTS $B_s$ in absolute tokens and never defines $N_q$; it makes its benefit case in user turns rather than in compute; and it cites Letta STC twice while filing it under "inference-time compute" and calling it reactive.

problem_stated.as_the_paper_frames_it: "While AI agents demonstrate remarkable capabilities in reasoning and tool use, they remain fundamentally reactive: they compute responses only after explicit user prompts. This paradigm ignores a critical opportunity: the idle time between interactions is largely wasted, leaving agents unable to prepare for future user needs." [Abstract, p.1]
problem_stated.the_counter_observation: "we argue that AI agents should view the idle time between user turns not as empty delay, but as an opportunity to anticipate, learn, and prepare for likely future demands." [§1, p.1]. And the operational form: "Instead of concentrating all computation at the moment of interaction, the agent shifts substantial work into off-peak periods." [§1, p.1]
problem_stated.the_operational_question: "The core challenge, then, is how to transform idle time into useful proactive work without overwhelming the user with irrelevant, premature, or weakly grounded suggestions (Lu et al., 2024; Lin et al., 2025)." [§1, p.1]. Note that this sentence is the first of the paper's two citations of Letta STC.
problem_stated.the_metaphor_it_actually_borrows: Not biology. Psychology: "This limitation contrasts with the psychological concept of proactive coping (Greenglass, 1999; Drummond and Brough, 2016), a future-oriented strategy in which individuals anticipate upcoming demands, accumulate resources, and prepare for prospective goals before those demands fully materialize." [§1, p.1]. Two of the 26 references are psychology papers on proactive coping; zero are neuroscience.
problem_stated.note_writer_remark: [note-writer] Like Letta STC, this paper manufactures its gap rather than inheriting one, and the manufactured gap has the same shape — an assumption imputed to a literature ('agents are reactive') that none of the cited works states as an open question. The two papers in the Precompute column are structurally identical in this respect and neither hands the other a question. See inherited_open_question.

inherited_open_question.justification: The paper quotes no prior work's open question anywhere. §2 (pp.2–3) is organised by technique family — 'Memory-augmented LLM agents', 'Proactive and anticipatory agents', 'Inference-time compute' — and every paragraph ends in a contrast clause of the form 'however, X remains reactive / lacks proactive anticipation / operates strictly on demand ... In contrast, ProAct ...'. No sentence of any cited paper is quoted, and no unresolved question is attributed to anyone.
inherited_open_question.the_substantive_but_unquoted_inheritance: Letta STC §7 (p.13) left exactly this: "An interesting direction for future work is identifying which contexts may have predictable questions and optimally allocating inference compute between sleep-time and test-time across different contexts and queries." ProAct answers the FIRST half of that sentence — it builds a predictor of which needs are anticipatable, gates on it, and measures the result (Anticipation Recall) — and it does so without quoting or acknowledging the sentence. It does not answer the second half: allocation of compute between sleep and wake is never optimised (see discriminant_verdict and unfavorable_facts).
inherited_open_question.and_it_removes_a_circularity_the_book_id: [note-writer] `letta-stc.json` systems_implications records that Letta STC's proposed predictability signal $\log P(q\mid c)$ cannot gate the sleep decision because it requires $q$, which is not available at sleep time, and that "the paper names the resulting problem as future work (§7, p.13) without observing this circularity". ProAct removes the circularity by construction: it does not score a known $q$, it GENERATES candidate $q$'s from $(H_t, M_t)$ and scores those [§3.2–3.3, pp.3–4]. This is a real, mechanically meaningful advance on the exact defect the book identified — delivered by a paper that never mentions the defect, the sentence, or the phrase 'sleep-time compute'.

core_mechanism.one_line_unified: ProAct instantiates (U-E) alone, but inserts a new operator IN FRONT of it: a predictor that manufactures the query the write is meant to serve. Where Letta STC computes $\hat c = S(c; B_s)$ on an existing context, ProAct computes $\hat c = S(\hat q; B_s)$ on a FORECAST of a query that has not been asked. $\Theta$ and $W$ are frozen throughout; nothing is trained anywhere in the paper.

what_is_NOT_in_the_mechanism: No learning of any kind. No gradient, optimizer, adapter, reward model, or trained scorer. Every weight and threshold in P3 and P5 is hand-set ($w=0.25$ each, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{conf}}=0.6$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}=60$, push 40 / high-priority 70) [App. C, p.13–14].
No solution to the stated objective P7. The $\lambda$'s are never numbered and $\pi$ is never optimised.

No decision about WHEN to sleep or HOW MUCH to spend. The idle window is a fixed simulated trigger — 'the simulated idle trigger is 5 seconds' [App. F, p.15] — and the search budget is a fixed configuration constant per run, swept only as an experimental variable.

No capacity bound, no eviction, no expiry. The only pressure on store growth is the deduplication lifecycle of Algorithm 1, and its skip/replace/merge decisions come from an unaudited LLM arbitration call whose accuracy is never measured [App. U, pp.24–25].

No cross-session or cross-scenario persistence. The word 'session' does not appear in the paper. Each ProActEval scenario is a self-contained closed world with its own fact sheet and its own store, so $E$ dies with the scenario exactly as Letta STC's $E$ dies with the context.

No open-world acquisition. Evidence 'search' operates over the scenario's own fact sheet: 'The system under test then responds using only runtime-visible information: the user profile, the fact sheet loaded into memory or search, and the conversation history.' [§4.3, p.6]. All entities are fictional [§4.1, p.6]. What idle-time compute buys is therefore selection and organisation of already-available facts, not the acquisition of unavailable ones.
No amortisation model. The word 'amortize' does not appear; $N_q$ has no counterpart; sleep cost is reported per scenario and never divided by anything.

outer_vs_inner.reader_takeaway: [note-writer] Read next to `letta-stc`, this table makes the E-path's shape unmistakable: three years apart, two papers in the same cell, and both have an empty outer-loop column. The E-path can still be demonstrated end-to-end without a single backward pass. What ProAct adds is not learning but PLUMBING — admission control, a write lifecycle, and a delivery gate — and the plumbing is where all of its constants live, unswept.

how_this_paper_differs_from_the_canonica: THE OPERAND OF $S$ IS A FORECAST, NOT A CONTEXT. Canonically $S$ re-represents a context $c$ that already exists. Here the context is used to manufacture a candidate query $\hat q$ first, and $S$ is then applied to $\hat q$: 'Predict likely future information needs after the current turn is answered. Do not predict facts that merely help answer the current user question.' [App. M, p.20]. S0's (U-E) has no slot for this predictor. The chapter must either add one or state explicitly that the frame is being extended.

$\mathrm{wr}$ IS A FIVE-WAY LIFECYCLE, NOT AN OVERWRITE. SHA-256 exact match → DUPLICATE; nearest-neighbour vector hit → LLM arbitration → SKIP / REPLACE / MERGE with `merged_into`/`merged_from` provenance; otherwise ADD [App. U, Algorithm 1, pp.24–25]. Compare the corpus: Letta STC = destructive overwrite; ReasoningBank = pure union; Mem0 = {ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, NOOP}. ProAct is the only one with content-hash dedup and provenance-preserving merge — and notably it has NO DELETE. Nothing is ever removed by policy.

$\mathrm{ret}$ IS A REAL RETRIEVER. Vector search over the store plus a temporal/sentiment index that 'retrieves messages within a configurable time window and highlights the closest temporal match' [App. J, p.17]. This is the first Precompute-column paper in which retrieval is not the identity map, so retrieval cost is exercised — and, uniquely in the corpus, MEASURED (Table 16, p.22).

ACQUISITION IS INCREMENTAL AND MEMORY-AWARE. Coverage of the store is checked before spending budget: high coverage → reuse, partial → search only missing subtopics, low → decompose into sub-questions and iterate [§3.4, p.5]. This is the corpus's first write path that reads its own store to decide how much to write.

THE WRITE IS GATED BEFORE IT IS PAID FOR. $\sigma(z)\ge\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}$ decides whether a candidate consumes budget at all; sub-threshold candidates are queued or stored without search [§3.4, p.5]. Letta STC has no admission control — it spends its budget unconditionally on every context.

MULTI-ROUND BY CONSTRUCTION. One idle window per turn boundary, roughly 5–8 rounds per scenario at T100 $\approx$ 6.9 turns. $k$ exceeds 1 in every scenario, unlike Letta STC where $k=1$ always. Repeated (U-E) application is therefore exercised — although no per-round degradation rate is reported (see cost_table.rho).

$E$ IS SCENARIO-SCOPED AND EPHEMERAL, exactly as Letta STC's store is context-scoped. No cross-session merge, no persistence beyond the conversation, no re-consolidation. The word 'session' does not occur in the paper.

conditions.evidence: Design statement: 'ProAct predicts upcoming needs and iteratively acquires information, allowing the agent to resolve knowledge gaps and prepare evidence before the user initiates a query.' [Abstract, p.1]. Mechanism statement: 'During an idle interval, Future-State Prediction generates a compact set of candidate future needs' [§3.1, p.3]. And the sharpest evidence, which is an operational constraint rather than a claim: 'Future-State Prediction runs after the current turn has been answered. Its job is not to retrieve facts for the current answer; it proposes predicted needs for Idle-Time Acquisition.' [App. M, p.20], implemented as the prompt line 'Predict likely future information needs after the current turn is answered. Do not predict facts that merely help answer the current user question.' [App. M, p.20].
conditions.what_weakens_it: Two things, both in the paper. (i) The idle interval is not real: 'the simulated idle trigger is 5 seconds' [App. F, p.15]. No real idle time is measured and no wall-clock separation between foreground and background work is reported. (ii) The paper's own end-to-end trace shows same-turn delivery: at Turn 2 of finance_basic_01, 'After answering, the predictor generates two candidates ... Both pass the confidence filter (≥ 0.6) and are approved for inline delivery. The assistant weaves facts F06–F09 into the response' [App. D, p.14], and Table 8 books the resulting coverage against Turn 2 itself. §3.4 by contrast says a queued artifact is 'queued for integration into a later response' [p.5]. The two passages do not agree.
conditions.resolution: [note-writer] Condition (1) survives, but only once it is indexed correctly, and the indexing is a genuine refinement the book does not currently state. The condition must be read against THE QUERY THE ARTIFACT SERVES, not against the wall-clock window in which the artifact is produced. Need N3 ('fees and minimum deposit') had not been asked when the evidence for it was prepared; that the evidence was then spliced into the reply to N2 does not make the work reactive with respect to N3. Under the wall-clock reading, ProAct would fall to MemGPT's boundary status and OUTLOOK §5.1 would survive; under the served-query reading it passes cleanly. The served-query reading is the correct one because it is the reading under which condition (1) does work — it is what separates a forecast from a record, and it is what the paper's own prompt enforces.

conditions.evidence_for: Anticipation Recall 0.428 (runtime fact-ID matching) / 0.447 (judge-labelled), against 0.000 for both baselines [Table 2, p.8; Table 3, p.8], where Anticipation Recall is 'the fraction of predictable needs covered before explicit request' [App. E, p.15]. Micro count: 703 of 1,572 predictable needs anticipated [Table 3, p.8; App. I, p.17].
conditions.evidence_against: 'Directed Idle records nonzero anticipation recall in 192 of 200 scenarios, but in 82 of those scenarios user effort does not decrease relative to Reactive.' [App. O, p.22] — i.e. in 42.7% of the scenarios where anticipation demonstrably happened, it produced no measurable downstream benefit. Worse: 'In 6 of 200 scenarios (3.0%), Directed Idle has smaller final must-have coverage than Reactive' [App. O, p.22], with the worst logged case going from total coverage 1.000 and $T_{100}=6$ under Reactive to total coverage 0.500 and $T_{100}=11$ under the full system [Table 13, p.19].
conditions.reading: [note-writer] The condition asks whether the change is USED, not whether the use helps. It passes. But the chapter must carry both halves, because this is the first corpus paper that measures the gap between 'the stored artifact was consumed' and 'consuming it improved the outcome' — and the gap is 43%.

discriminant_verdict.which_condition_decides: Condition (1). Conditions (2), (3) and (4) are satisfied on any reading and were never in doubt: tokens are spent and printed, $E$ moves, and the movement is retrieved. Condition (1) is the only contestable one, and it is also the only one that determines the COLUMN: if the idle work were indexed to the wall-clock window rather than to the served need, ProAct would sit beside MemGPT as a boundary case and the Precompute column would still hold one paper. Indexed to the served need — the reading the paper's own predictor prompt enforces — it passes, and the printed sentence in OUTLOOK §5.1 fails.
discriminant_verdict.what_it_does_NOT_change: The other three empty cells of the OUTLOOK §5.1 grid are untouched. ProAct is $E$; Precompute×$W$ and Precompute×$\Theta$ remain at zero, and Dreaming×$E$ and Dreaming×$W$ remain at zero. The finding is one cell going from one member to two, not a redistribution.
discriminant_verdict.count_procedure_ch24_F6: ch24 §24.5 F6 asks how many of the four conditions a new paper's own definition sentence makes explicit. ProAct scores 4/4 — the highest in the corpus, against SleepGate's 0/4. (1) 'before the user initiates a query' [Abstract, p.1]; (2) 'leverages idle-time compute' with the quantity metered in Table 2; (3) 'generates compact knowledge artifacts, and commits them to memory' [§1, p.2]; (4) 'these insights can be proactively delivered, woven into subsequent responses, or silently retrieved the moment the user's anticipated need materializes' [§1, p.2]. [본서 관찰] No other paper in the corpus states all four.

B_s.value: PRESENT — 111.8k active tokens per scenario (full system); 69.8k (undirected ablation); 0 (reactive baseline)
B_s.detail: Reported twice, in Table 2 ('Active Tokens ↓', p.8) and Table 10 ('Compute and resource disclosure', p.17), with the accounting boundary defined in App. E (p.15): proactive runtime modules only, excluding reactive response generation, simulator, judge and evaluation-only push scoring. Wall-clock is also printed per scenario-condition: 264.8 s reactive, 660.8 s undirected, 687.2 s directed [Table 10, p.17]. Budget-sweep knob: $\kappa_{\mathrm{search}}\in\{4,8,12,16\}$ on a matched 50-scenario subset, with active-token cost plotted in Figure 3 panel (d) [§5.3, p.8; Fig. 3, p.9]. Main-run configuration constants: per-search query budget 1, per-idle intent limit 3, condition name 'Full-single-idle' [App. F, p.15].
B_s.what_is_still_missing: No FLOPs and no conversion to FLOPs, because gpt-4o's parameter count is undisclosed — the same wall that X3 Q2 hit with ReasoningBank. No breakdown of the 111.8k across the five pipeline stages. No per-turn or per-idle-window figure. The numeric values behind Figure 3(d) are not printed in the text; the only budget-swept numbers stated in prose are Anticipation Recall 0.253 at $\kappa=4$ and 0.432 at $\kappa=16$ [§5.3, p.8].
B_s.derived: [본서 산술] 111.8k active tokens buys $\Delta T_{100}=1.200$ turns and $\Delta$User Effort $=1.065$ turns, i.e. $\approx$93.2k active tokens per turn of completion saved and $\approx$105.0k per user turn saved; and $703/200=3.515$ anticipated needs per scenario, i.e. $\approx$31.8k active tokens per anticipated need. None of these three ratios appears in the paper.

L_w.value: PARTIAL — the first wake-side latency numbers in the corpus, but not for the wake response
L_w.detail: Table 16 (p.22) prints memory-operation latency in seconds per operation: ProAct read $\sim$0.04 s, write $\sim$0.06 s, against FullMemory $<$0.001/$<$0.001, RecentMemory $<$0.001/$<$0.001, RetrievalMemory 0.036/0.057, GenerativeAgent 0.028/6.064, MemoryBank 0.033/15.705, MemGPT 1.042/$<$0.001, SCMemory 0.036/0.057. 'Read latency measures time to recall relevant memory for a query; write latency measures time to store a new memory entry.' [§N preamble, p.21].
L_w.what_is_still_missing: No TTFT, no ms/token, no end-to-end response latency, no separation of idle wall-clock from foreground wall-clock inside the 687.2 s figure. The read latency is the retrieval step alone, not the wake-time contribution of the whole memory subsystem; and the acquisition pipeline that produces 111.8k tokens is not in Table 16 at all, so Table 16 must not be read as the cost of the memory system.
L_w.note_for_the_book: [note-writer] ch25 §25.2.1's printed claim is that no paper in the corpus reports $L_w$ in the required unit. Table 16 is a genuine partial counter-example — seconds per read operation is a wake-latency contribution in a usable unit — and the book must either amend the claim to 'one paper, partially' or state why a per-operation retrieval latency is not $L_w$. It cannot be left as it stands. See book_impact.

C.detail: No byte count, no character count, no token count for the store or for any artifact. Whole-text grep for 'byte' returns exactly one hit and it is the size of an evaluation trace file ('the 104 MB trace file', App. F, p.15), not state. The corpus statistics that exist — mean 30.6 facts and 12.4 needs per scenario [Fig. 4(a)(b), p.26] — describe the benchmark, not the store. No capacity bound, no growth curve, no per-user or per-session figure.
C.finding: The one E-path paper that reports its sleep budget still does not report its state size. PRE-RESEARCH §4's 'corpus 전체에서 상태 용량을 바이트로 보고한 논문이 0편' survives this paper intact.

rho.value: absent as a rate — but the degradation SIGNAL is present, measured, and named, which is new
rho.detail: Multiple sleep rounds occur per scenario (one per turn boundary), so unlike Letta STC repetition is exercised. The paper does not compute a per-round degradation rate. What it does report: (i) 6 of 200 scenarios (3.0%) end with lower must-have coverage than the reactive baseline, named 'Reactive compatibility regression' [App. O, p.22]; (ii) a worked catastrophic case, total coverage 1.000→0.500 and $T_{100}$ 6→11 [Table 13, p.19]; (iii) budget non-monotonicity — 'active-token cost rises steadily while T100 and User Effort flatten or fluctuate' [§5.3, p.8]; (iv) 5 of 40 domains with non-negative $\Delta T_{100}$, three of them strictly worse at +0.4 turns [Table 11, pp.18–19].
rho.why_it_is_not_rho: All four are within-run, cross-scenario or cross-budget effects, not a measured loss per consolidation round. The book's $\rho$ asks what one more sleep round costs the state; ProAct asks what one more search costs the conversation. Related, not the same quantity.

N_q.value: NOT DEFINED, and — this is the structural point — the paper's benefit runs in the OPPOSITE DIRECTION on it
N_q.detail: The word 'amortize' does not appear. There is no per-query cost, no division of sleep cost by anything, and no analogue of identity (A). Sleep cost is reported per scenario. The nearest quantities are 7.86 predictable needs per scenario (1,572/200) and 12.4 needs per scenario [Fig. 4(d), p.26; Fig. 4(a), p.26].
N_q.the_inversion: [본서 추론] Letta STC wins by making $N_q$ LARGE — $C_{\mathrm{avg}}=\kappa_{\mathrm{cost}}B_t+B_s/N_q$, so more queries per context is better. ProAct's primary endpoint is User Effort, defined as the number of turns in which the user must explicitly ask [App. E, p.15], and the mechanism that improves it is the simulator SKIPPING a need that was already covered [§4.3, p.6]. ProAct is therefore paid for making $N_q$ SMALL. The two members of the Precompute column have opposite signs on the denominator of the book's own amortisation identity, and identity (A) cannot represent the second one at all.
N_q.and_the_compute_goes_up: ProAct never claims a compute saving. Total compute strictly increases (0 → 111.8k active tokens; 264.8 s → 687.2 s wall-clock) and the conclusion says so: 'larger Idle-Time Acquisition budgets raise active-token cost and yield diminishing returns, so proactive computation is an operating-point trade-off rather than something to maximize.' [§6, p.9]. This is the first paper in the corpus whose sleep-time compute is not a cost argument in any form.

experiments.result_tables_exist: Yes — 19 tables and 4 figures, with paired bootstrap 95% CIs for every main delta [Table 9, p.16]. This is by a wide margin the most completely tabulated paper in the E-path corpus; Letta STC has one table and it is dataset statistics.

scale_ceiling.model_size: Unknown by construction for the main results: gpt-4o and gpt-4o-mini are closed APIs with undisclosed parameter counts, and the assistant model is never named separately from the simulator. The only stated size in the paper is Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, used only on the MemBench arm [§5.2, p.8]. No model-scale sweep of any kind.
scale_ceiling.evaluation_scale: 200 scenarios × 3 conditions on ProActEval, with 1,685 turns logged for the ProactiveAgent comparison arm [App. I, p.17]; 400 trajectories (10k) and 80 trajectories (100k) on MemBench [Table 10, p.17]. Budget sweep on a 50-scenario subset only.
scale_ceiling.context_length_ceiling: ProActEval scenarios carry a mean of 30.6 facts and 12.4 needs and run to T100 $\approx$ 6.9 turns — a short conversation by any deployment standard. The only long-context evidence is the MemBench 100k arm, which is 80 trajectories on a 7B model. No context-length sweep on the paper's own benchmark.
scale_ceiling.realism_ceiling: Everything is synthetic and closed-world. All entities are fictional; the fact sheet is the entire universe of admissible content; 'search' resolves against that sheet rather than against the open web; the user is an LLM simulator; the verdict is an LLM judge; and both the need graph and the definition of what is 'predictable' are authored by the same pipeline that the system is scored against. The paper states the first of these plainly in its Limitations [§6, p.9].
scale_ceiling.deployment_gap: [note-writer] The motivating scenario in Figure 1 is a knowledge worker preparing a real project review across a real repository of project state over a real multi-day idle window. What is evaluated is a 6-turn synthetic dialogue with a 5-second simulated idle trigger and a 30-fact closed universe. The same gap, in the same direction, as `letta-stc`'s (codebases motivated, 33 PRs evaluated).

book_impact.summary: One printed sentence is BROKEN, three printed census/accounting claims are THREATENED, four are CONFIRMED, and one condition of the discriminant needs a stated refinement. Nothing in the book's spine judgment (A1) is overturned, but two of its three supporting clauses now need qualification rather than repetition.

overturned.the_printed_sentence: "**Precompute 열은 여전히 한 편이다.** [문서]가 '원 논문은 왼쪽 Precompute 하나에 가까웠다'고 쓴 것은 맞고, **2026-08 기준으로도 그 열은 그 한 편뿐이다.** $W$나 $\Theta$에서 질의 전 예상 계산을 한 논문이 0편이다."
overturned.what_conflicts: ProAct occupies Precompute×$E$ alongside Letta STC. Its idle-time work is indexed to a query that has not been asked — the predictor is explicitly forbidden from serving the current one ('Do not predict facts that merely help answer the current user question' [App. M, p.20]) — and the resulting artifact is written to persistent memory and consumed later. That is precomputation, not consolidation: the write is a forecast, not a record of what happened.
overturned.what_survives: The second sentence stands unchanged. ProAct is $E$; Precompute×$W$ and Precompute×$\Theta$ are still zero, and the grid still has four empty cells. The correct amendment is one cell going from one member to two, plus a note that the column's two members are three years and one (mis-)citation apart and share no chain.
overturned.consequence_for_the_recommended_grid: OUTLOOK §5.4's recommendation — 'ch24에 층 × 목적 2차 격자를 부록 표로 신설한다 ... 격자의 빈 칸 넷을 명시한다' — is unaffected in form and must be re-populated in content. Reading 3 of §5.1 ('Consolidation 행만 세 층을 덮는다') also survives.

overturned.the_printed_sentence: "$B_s$ | **절대 FLOPs 또는 토큰으로 인쇄한 논문 1편**(ReasoningBank, 과제당 3748.4 토큰)이고, 그 1편조차 backbone 크기가 없어 FLOPs로 환산되지 않는다[X3 Q1, Q2]. 19편 침묵, 그중 9편은 $B_s$가 **정의조차 되지 않는다**"
overturned.what_conflicts: '1편' becomes '2편'. ProAct prints 111.8k / 69.8k / 0 active tokens per scenario in two separate tables [Table 2, p.8; Table 10, p.17], with the sleep/wake accounting boundary defined in prose [App. E, p.15], plus wall-clock 264.8 / 660.8 / 687.2 s.
overturned.what_survives: The rest of the row survives exactly. gpt-4o's parameter count is undisclosed, so the tokens still do not convert to FLOPs — the same wall as ReasoningBank, for the same reason. The count of papers whose $B_s$ is convertible to FLOPs remains zero.
overturned.why_this_one_matters_most: ProAct's definition is cleaner than ReasoningBank's: it names exactly which modules count as sleep and which do not, and it excludes the reactive response generation from the sleep total. That is the first explicit sleep/wake accounting boundary in the corpus, and X3 should adopt its shape.

A per-query retrieval time in seconds IS a wake-latency contribution in a usable unit.
threatened.the_case_for_holding_the_claim: It is not TTFT, not ms/token, not the latency of a wake response, and not the latency of any staging path in 표 29-4. It measures one component (the store's read op) of one system, in seconds rather than ms, with a tilde on the paper's own two values and three decimals on everyone else's.

threatened.target: OUTLOOK-REVIEW §3 U1 as a whole — the scheduler objective
threatened.the_printed_sentence: "**값이 없다.** 다섯 항 중 하나도 오늘 수로 채워지지 않는다. 최적화는커녕 목적함수를 **평가**할 수 없다." and "$I_{\mathrm{interference}}$ | **대응 칸 없음** ... 양쪽 코퍼스가 함께 비어 있는 유일한 항이다 (O7)"
threatened.what_conflicts: ProAct §3.2 (p.4) prints a four-term metacontroller objective of the same shape — future utility minus interruption cost, budget cost and hallucination risk — and puts numbers on two of its terms in the same paper: budget = 111.8k active tokens [Table 2, p.8] and hallucination = 0.095 [Table 2, p.8]. It also gives the interruption term the corpus's first operationalisation: PushScore $=\mathrm{clip}(V-C+50,0,100)$ with a push threshold of 40 and a high-priority band at 70, plus a one-artifact-per-window rate limit [App. C, p.14].
threatened.what_survives_and_it_is_most_of_it: $\lambda_i,\lambda_b,\lambda_h$ are never assigned values; $\pi$ is never optimised by any procedure; the shipped gates are hand-set constants; there is no footprint term at all; and the interruption cost's 'unit' is an LLM-assigned 0–100 score, which is a proxy, not a unit. So O7's core claim — that the interference quantity has no unit in either corpus — survives. What fails is the stronger sentence that no term can be filled: two can, and are.
threatened.required_rewrite: The diagnosis must move from 'the objective does not exist and nothing can be filled' to 'the objective now exists in print, two of its four terms carry measured values, and what is still missing is the conversion coefficients and any act of optimisation'. That is a smaller gap than the book currently states, and stating it smaller makes it a sharper research target.

threatened.what_conflicts: ProAct is a metacontroller for WHAT to precompute (the value gate $\sigma(z)\ge\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}$ over relevance / knowledge gap / incremental value / timeliness, with a confidence prefilter and a cap of three candidates per window) and for WHETHER TO DELIVER (the push gate). Both are shipped, both are ablated, and the ablation is decisive: without predictive direction the same machinery spends 69.8k tokens for a 0.9% T100 improvement [§5.1, p.7].
threatened.what_survives: The 'when' is untouched. The idle trigger is a fixed simulated 5 seconds [App. F, p.15] and the budget $\kappa_{\mathrm{search}}$ is a configuration constant that the paper explicitly declines to optimise: 'the search budget should be treated as an operating point ... rather than as a parameter to maximize' [§5.3, p.8]. Letta STC's allocation question is therefore half-answered and half-open, and the book should say which half.
threatened.amendment: A3 should read: 'what to precompute and whether to interrupt now have a shipped controller; when to sleep and how much budget to spend do not.'

threatened.target: PRE-RESEARCH §1 and §5 — the E-path pattern that the quality winner is 'no memory system'

threatened.why_the_threat_is_weak: Three reasons, and the chapter must give all three. (i) The baselines are 'aggregate reflective accuracy from the published MemBench results' [Table 14 caption, p.21] — not re-run under ProAct's Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct setup, so backbone comparability is unestablished. Auto-Dreamer's counter-example was a re-run under a shared frozen agent; this one is not. (ii) The 100k arm is 80 trajectories with no confidence intervals. (iii) On the paper's OWN benchmark there is no memoryless arm at all — Reactive disables the two proactive modules and keeps the memory layer [§5.1, p.7; App. S, p.24] — so ProActEval measures the marginal value of anticipation on top of a memory system and never measures the memory system.

new_findings_the_book_does_not_yet_state.detail: OUTLOOK O7 records $I_{\mathrm{interference}}$ as 'the only item both corpora leave empty'. ProAct gives it a gate — PushScore $=\mathrm{clip}(V-C+50,0,100)$, push at $\ge$40, high priority at $\ge$70, at most one push per idle window [App. C, p.14] — and makes it one of four terms in a printed objective [§3.2, p.4]. The quantity remains unit-less (an LLM assigns $V$ and $C$ on 0–100), so O7's core survives; but the item is no longer unnamed and unhandled. new_findings_the_book_does_not_yet_state.where_it_belongs: ch29 and ch30 — the book's four cost symbols are machine costs; a sleep-time system that pushes has a fifth, and the corpus now contains one implementation of a gate on it.

new_findings_the_book_does_not_yet_state.finding: THE E-PATH'S FIRST WRITE LIFECYCLE WITH CONTENT-HASH DEDUP AND PROVENANCE-PRESERVING MERGE — AND NO DELETE.
new_findings_the_book_does_not_yet_state.detail: Algorithm 1 (App. U, pp.24–25): SHA-256 exact match → nearest-neighbour vector search → LLM arbitration returning skip/replace/merge, with `merged_into`/`merged_from` pointers. Against the corpus: Letta STC = destructive overwrite, ReasoningBank = pure union, Mem0 = {ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, NOOP}, Auto-Dreamer = region replacement. ProAct is the only one that preserves merge provenance, and the only one with no deletion primitive at all. Since REPLACE is destructive and unaudited, a wrong arbitration is unrecoverable — the same failure shape ch15 records for Mem0's DELETE, arrived at from the opposite direction.
new_findings_the_book_does_not_yet_state.where_it_belongs: ch15's $\mathrm{wr}$ taxonomy and ch27's T8 row ('파괴적 쓰기가 미검증 판정기와 결합한다').

new_findings_the_book_does_not_yet_state.finding: A MEASURED GAP BETWEEN 'THE ARTIFACT WAS USED' AND 'USING IT HELPED' — 43%.
new_findings_the_book_does_not_yet_state.detail: 'Directed Idle records nonzero anticipation recall in 192 of 200 scenarios, but in 82 of those scenarios user effort does not decrease relative to Reactive.' new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.definition: compute spent in the interval between user turns to anticipate and prepare for needs the user has not yet voiced
new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.note: A second name for the same operational move as 'sleep-time compute', coined by a paper that cites 'sleep-time compute' and does not use the phrase. The book's naming diagnosis (ch24 판정 2, '이름이 기제보다 넓다') now has a companion symptom: the mechanism has more names than it has papers.

new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.definition: the operator $f_{\mathrm{pred}}(H,E)\to\hat Q$ that manufactures candidate future queries from dialogue history and persistent memory, in two classes (NEXT-STEP within topic, ADJACENT from long-range profile) plus a memory-gap injection path
new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.note: The operator S0's (U-E) has no slot for. This is the paper's real contribution and the reason it sits in the Precompute column.

new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.definition: converting the memory layer's own findings of 'stale, incomplete, weakly supported, or missing knowledge' into candidate future needs, so that maintenance shapes acquisition targets
new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.note: The corpus's first mechanism in which the store's deficiencies become sleep-time work items — an $E$-path analogue of curiosity-driven exploration.

new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.definition: $\sigma(z)=w_r r+w_g g+w_v v+w_\tau\tau \ge \epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}$ — admission control deciding which predicted needs consume sleep budget
new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.note: The first admission-control rule for sleep-time work in the corpus. Letta STC spends unconditionally.
Admission control on the OUTPUT channel, gating on a cost borne by the user rather than by the machine.

new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.note: The corpus's first metric that scores a memory system on what it produced BEFORE being asked. Reported in two incompatible variants in the same paper (0.428 runtime fact-ID vs 0.447 judge-labelled).

new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.definition: the number of turns in which the user must explicitly ask for an unmet need

unfavorable_facts.fact: Everything is closed-world synthetic and the evidence the agent 'acquires' is already inside the scenario. 'The system under test then responds using only runtime-visible information: the user profile, the fact sheet loaded into memory or search, and the conversation history.' All entities — people, organizations, addresses, dates, emails, internal URLs — are fictional.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: idle-time compute therefore buys SELECTION and ORGANISATION of facts already available to the baseline, not the acquisition of facts that were unavailable. The headline is a claim about anticipating needs, and the experiment cannot separate that from a claim about volunteering more of a sheet everyone can see.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The benchmark defines what counts as anticipatable, and the paper's flagship metric scores the system against that definition. The `predictable_after` links, importance labels, reveal groups and the user-needs graph are all authored by the same LLM-plus-manual pipeline that produced the scenarios.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Anticipation Recall 0.428 measures agreement with author-declared predictability. This is the same circularity class the book records for Letta STC's SWE-Features, where the model family that solves the task also defines its context.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The primary endpoint is produced by LLMs on both sides. A gpt-4o user simulator decides which need to voice and which to skip; a gpt-4o-mini coverage judge decides which facts were conveyed, distorted or hallucinated and which needs were addressed; the assistant is from the same vendor family.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: User Effort — the metric that carries the paper's user-facing claim — is definitionally whatever the judge says was covered. The paper concedes 'The evaluation also depends on an LLM judge' but reports no judge-accuracy measurement, no human agreement study, and no judge ablation.

unfavorable_facts.fact: One run, one seed. 'The seed is 42.' The bootstrap resamples SCENARIOS with replacement, not runs.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: every confidence interval in Table 9 describes scenario-sampling variance only. LLM run-to-run stochasticity — which the closed-loop design amplifies, since each condition 'induces a different closed-loop trajectory' by the paper's own account — is outside every interval printed.

unfavorable_facts.fact: There is no memoryless or full-context arm on the paper's own benchmark. 'Reactive is a non-proactive baseline that disables both Future-State Prediction and Idle-Time Acqisition' — the memory layer stays on in all three conditions.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: ProActEval measures the marginal value of anticipation on top of a memory system and never measures the memory system. ch27's FE2 requirement is unmet, so the corpus's standing question — whether the memory system beats no memory system — is again not asked where it would have been cheapest to ask.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The paper's own showcase trace gets the majority of its improvement from a turn in which the proactive pipeline did not run. 'The proactive gate is skipped at Turn 1 due to a minimum-conversation-turn threshold ... However, the assistant's reactive response naturally covers the employer match (N1, F20) and proactively mentions the enrollment portal (N6, F26–F27) and the vesting schedule (N9, F21) ... covers 3 of 12 needs in a single turn, compared with Reactive's 0/12 after Turn 1.' The paper then attributes the trace's 3-turn saving to two sources, the first of which is 'cross-group anticipation in Turn 1 eliminates separate turns for N6 and N9'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: two of the three saved turns arise at a turn where the method is disabled, which means the two arms differ in their reactive response behaviour by something other than idle-time compute. Either the response prompts differ between conditions — in which case the arms are not matched — or the same model produced 3/12 and 0/12 on identical inputs, in which case the trace is a variance sample presented as a mechanism demonstration. The paper does not resolve which.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The paper contradicts itself about when a prepared artifact is delivered. §3.4 says a queued artifact is 'queued for integration into a later response'; App. D's trace says the turn-2 candidates were 'approved for inline delivery' and that 'The assistant weaves facts F06–F09 into the response', booking the coverage against turn 2 itself.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: this is the difference between idle compute that sits off the wake critical path and idle compute that sits on it. If the artifact is spliced into the same reply, the acquisition latency is wake latency, and the book's touchstone — sleep contributes zero to $L_w$ — is violated for that mode. The paper reports no latency that would settle it.
unfavorable_facts.source: [§3.4, p.5 against App. D, p.14; Table 8, p.15]

unfavorable_facts.fact: Two different Anticipation Recall values are reported for the same run: 0.428 (runtime fact-ID matching, Table 2) and 0.447 (judge-labelled, Table 3).
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the paper's headline novel metric moves by 4.4% relative depending on which of its own instruments reads it, and the paper switches instruments between the ablation table and the comparison table without reporting the agreement between them.
unfavorable_facts.source: [Table 2, p.8; Table 3, p.8; App. I, p.17]

unfavorable_facts.fact: Table 3's 'scenario-level macro average' reproduces the micro ratio exactly for both systems: 703/1,572 = 0.4472 against a printed 0.447, and 32/1,572 = 0.02036 against a printed 0.020.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: a macro average over 200 scenarios with unequal need counts would not generally equal the micro ratio to three decimals for both systems at once. Either the label is wrong or the scenarios are unusually homogeneous; the caption asserts the former reading without evidence. [본서 산술]

unfavorable_facts.fact: The comparison baseline anticipates almost nothing yet captures most of the turn improvement. ProactiveAgent reaches $T_{100}=7.145$ against Reactive's 8.110 — a 0.965-turn improvement — with a judge-labelled Anticipation Recall of 0.020. ProAct reaches 6.910 with 0.447.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the metric the paper introduces moves 22×; the metric a user would feel moves 0.235 turns (3.3%) further. [본서 산술] And the baseline achieving that was handed the entire fact sheet at every turn — 'The prompt therefore exposes all scenario facts at every turn' — while ProAct was not. The paper's own thesis, that anticipation of benchmark-labelled needs is what reduces effort, is weakened by its own comparison table.
unfavorable_facts.source: [Table 2, p.8; Table 3, p.8; App. I, p.17]

unfavorable_facts.fact: Anticipation and benefit decouple in 43% of the anticipating scenarios. 'Directed Idle records nonzero anticipation recall in 192 of 200 scenarios, but in 82 of those scenarios user effort does not decrease relative to Reactive.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: 82/192 = 42.7%. The paper credits itself with the decoupling as a benchmark-design insight, which is fair, but the same number is a direct discount on its headline mechanism story.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Proactive work makes the outcome strictly worse in a measured fraction of cases. 6 of 200 scenarios (3.0%) end with lower must-have coverage than Reactive; 5 of 40 domains have non-negative $\Delta T_{100}$ with three strictly worse (construction_site 8.0→8.4, negotiation 9.4→9.8, school_transport 7.0→7.4); and the logged worst case goes from total coverage 1.000 and $T_{100}=6$ under Reactive to 0.500 and $T_{100}=11$ under the full system.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: a halving of coverage on a task the baseline completes perfectly is a serious failure mode for a system whose delivery gate exists precisely to prevent it. The gate did not prevent it, and the anticipation recall in that run was a healthy 0.300.
unfavorable_facts.source: [App. O, p.22; Table 11, pp.18–19; App. L and Table 13, p.19]

unfavorable_facts.fact: The headline hallucination result is a relative reduction of a 3.7-percentage-point absolute difference, and the residual rate is 9.5% in a world where every admissible fact is handed to the system. Fact Accuracy 0.985 additionally means 1.5% of delivered facts are distorted.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: 'cuts hallucination rates by 28.1%' reads as a factuality result; 0.132 → 0.095 in a closed universe of about 30 supplied facts reads as one unsupported claim in every eleven, with an LLM judge deciding which. The abstract carries the relative form only.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The primary efficiency metric is right-censored with an imputed value, and neither the horizon nor the number of censored runs is reported. 'If a condition does not reach the target within the conversation horizon, we assign the horizon plus one.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: $T_{100}$ is the headline. Both logged example traces show a $T_{100}$ of 11 (one Reactive, one Directed Idle), which is consistent with a horizon of 10 and an imputed 11 [본서 추론]. If the Reactive arm censors more often than the Directed arm, the 14.8% improvement is partly an artifact of the imputation rule, and the paper gives the reader no way to check.
unfavorable_facts.source: [App. E, p.15; Table 12 and Table 13, p.19]

unfavorable_facts.fact: MemBench baselines are borrowed, not re-run, and Table 1's single 'Baseline' column silently switches systems between rows. 'Baseline numbers are aggregate reflective accuracy from the published MemBench results.' The 10k baseline of 0.742 is GenerativeAgent; the 100k baseline of 0.833 is RetrievalMemory.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: ProAct runs Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct locally; the published baselines' backbone is not stated anywhere in this paper, so the 'state-of-the-art reflective accuracy' claim rests on a comparison whose comparability is unestablished. And presenting a best-of-eight selection as 'Baseline' converts a max over eight systems into a single number with a '+13.6%' attached.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The MemBench evidence is thin where it is strongest. The 100k arm is 80 trajectories with no confidence intervals; the 10k run's token totals were not recorded; both run on a laptop ('a 10-core Apple M5 chip and 16 GB unified memory').
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the 100k margin over the best baseline is 0.030 (0.863 vs 0.833) on 80 trajectories with no dispersion statistic of any kind.

unfavorable_facts.fact: In the memory-efficiency table the paper's own system is the only row given approximately. ProAct is '∼0.04' read and '∼0.06' write; all seven baselines are printed to three decimals.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the one place where the corpus finally gets a wake-side latency number, it is the least precisely stated entry in its own table. And Table 16 measures only the store's read/write operation, not the 111.8k-token acquisition pipeline, so it must not be quoted as the cost of the memory system.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The write lifecycle's decisions are unaudited LLM calls with no measured accuracy and no recovery path. Algorithm 1 routes every non-exact-duplicate through `LLM_Arbitrate` returning skip/replace/merge, and REPLACE overwrites the existing entry in place.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: no accuracy, no false-replace rate, no ablation of the arbitration step, and no DELETE primitive — so a wrong REPLACE is unrecoverable and a wrong SKIP is silent. This is the defect class the book already records for Mem0's unaudited DELETE and ReasoningBank's 72.7% judge, appearing again in the newest paper in the column.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Every constant in the shipped controller is hand-set and unswept: $w_r=w_g=w_v=w_\tau=0.25$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{conf}}=0.6$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}=60$, push threshold 40, high-priority 70, at most three candidates per window.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the paper's contribution is a gate, and no sensitivity analysis of any gate parameter is reported. The only swept quantity is the search budget, on a 50-scenario subset.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The headline configuration is not located on the swept budget axis. The 200-scenario main run uses 'per-search query budget is 1, per-idle intent limit 3' under the condition name 'Full-single-idle'; the sweep uses $k\in\{4,8,12,16\}$ on a different, 50-scenario subset.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the cost–quality curve and the headline point are produced by different configurations on different data, so the reader cannot place the headline on the curve.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The idle window is fictional. 'the simulated idle trigger is 5 seconds.' No real idle time is measured, and the wall-clock figures in Table 10 (264.8 / 660.8 / 687.2 s per scenario-condition) do not separate background work from foreground work.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the entire premise is that idle time is free capacity. Nothing in the paper measures whether the work fits in an idle window, how long the pipeline takes, or what happens when the user returns mid-acquisition.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Three different decision sets appear for the same two gates. The acquisition prompt returns 'decision in {search_now, queue, store_only, drop}' [App. M, p.21]; §3.4 describes only retention below threshold ('Candidates below the threshold may be retained for later consideration'); Figure 2 and §3.4 give delivery as {push, queue, store}. 'drop' appears only in the prompt.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: whether sub-threshold candidates are dropped or retained changes what the store accumulates, which is the paper's own state variable.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Letta STC is cited twice and characterised as reactive. In §2 under 'Inference-time compute': 'recent test-time computation methods show that additional reasoning can improve performance on difficult tasks (Lin et al., 2025; Zhang et al., 2026; Gupta et al., 2024; Gao et al., 2025). However, these methods remain reactive: additional computation is triggered only after a user has issued a request, and is used to improve the response to that request rather than to anticipate and prepare for future user needs during idle periods.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Letta STC's defining property is that its computation is triggered BEFORE a request is issued, and its own abstract says so. The second paper in the Precompute column reads the first as belonging to the reactive literature it is displacing. This is not silence — it is a misfiling, and it is the reason ProAct believes it is introducing the paradigm.
unfavorable_facts.source: [§2, p.3; against Letta STC Abstract and §3, pp.1–4]

unfavorable_facts.fact: The word 'sleep' occurs exactly once in the whole paper — inside the bibliography entry for Letta STC. 'consolidation', 'offline', 'amortize', 'session' and 'byte' occur zero times.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: a paper that spends 111.8k tokens per conversation on pre-query computation, cites the paper that named that activity, and never once uses the name — while there is a growing corpus organised under it. [본서 관찰, whole-text grep]

unfavorable_facts.fact: Editorial slips cluster in the method text. §5.1 spells 'Idle-Time Acqisition' three times in the paragraph that defines the three experimental conditions; §1 duplicates 'on ProActEval' inside a single sentence stating three headline numbers.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: minor in itself, but it is the same pattern the book records for Letta STC, where the least carefully typeset sentence was the one stating the adverse result — here it is the sentence defining what the ablation arms are.

credits_where_due: Paired nonparametric bootstrap 95% CIs for every main delta, with the resampling procedure, count (10,000) and seed (2026) stated [App. G, p.16]. No other $E$-path paper in the corpus does this.

A compute-and-resource table with active tokens AND wall-clock for all three conditions, and an explicit definition of what counts [App. E, p.15; Table 10, p.17]. This is the printed value the book has been asking twenty-nine papers for.

A failure-mode appendix that counts its own regressions (6/200), names the decoupling of anticipation from effort (82/192), and publishes a trace in which the method halves coverage [App. O, p.22; Table 13, p.19].
A per-domain table that shows the five domains where the method does not help [Table 11, pp.18–19], and a stratification table that flags its own strongest cell as n=3 [Table 17, p.23].

An ablation that isolates the paper's actual claim: idle-time compute without predictive direction spends 69.8k tokens for a 0.9% improvement, so the contribution is the direction and not the compute [§5.1, p.7].

A limitations paragraph that states the closed-world caveat, the judge dependence and the backfire mode in plain terms [§6, p.9], and a broader-impacts section that names the surveillance risk of persistent future-need prediction [App. P, p.23].

cross_path_citations.verdict: Total silence toward the $W$-path and the $\Theta$-path; total silence toward biology and CLS; a psychology citation where the biology would be; and — uniquely in the corpus — a citation of the founding paper of its own path that MISCLASSIFIES it.

E_path_internal.citations: Dense and current: MemGPT (Packer et al. 2023), Generative Agents (Park et al. 2023), MemoryBank (Zhong et al. 2024), SCMemory (Wang et al. 2023a), GAM (Yan et al. 2025), plus five memory benchmarks (MemBench, LongMemEval, MemSim, PerLTQA, DialSim) and two proactive-agent works (Proactive Agent, ProactiveBench).
E_path_internal.what_is_missing_inside_the_path: Mem0, Zep, ReasoningBank, SCM, Auto-Dreamer, RAG — none appear. The paper's $E$-path ancestry is the agent-memory-architecture line only, not the memory-consolidation line the book groups with it.

the_letta_stc_citation.occurrences: Exactly two, both parenthetical, neither discussing the mechanism. (i) §1, p.1: 'The core challenge, then, is how to transform idle time into useful proactive work without overwhelming the user with irrelevant, premature, or weakly grounded suggestions (Lu et al., 2024; Lin et al., 2025).' (ii) §2, p.3, under the heading 'Inference-time compute', where it is grouped with three unrelated works and then declared reactive.
the_letta_stc_citation.the_misfiling: 'However, these methods remain reactive: additional computation is triggered only after a user has issued a request, and is used to improve the response to that request rather than to anticipate and prepare for future user needs during idle periods.' [§2, p.3]. That sentence is false of Letta STC and true of the other three cited works. Letta STC's abstract reads 'sleep-time compute, where we allow models to "think" offline about contexts before queries are presented'.
the_letta_stc_citation.why_this_is_the_finding: [note-writer] PRE-RESEARCH §3.1 distinguishes silence forced by chronology from silence that is chosen. This is neither. It is a third category the map does not yet have: CITED AND MISREAD. The consequence is concrete — because ProAct believes the pre-query line does not exist, it introduces a second name ('idle-time compute'), rebuilds the same move from psychology instead of from the prior paper, and hands the book a Precompute column with two members and no chain. The silence map needs a fourth column state, and the chapter should say that a misfiling propagates further than an omission, because an omission leaves the reader free to look.

W_path.citations: ZERO. No fast weights, no test-time training, no Titans/Miras/Atlas, no linear attention, no state-space models, no recurrent memory. 'KV cache' does not appear; 'state' appears only in 'future-state' and 'memory state'.

Theta_path.citations: ZERO. No LoRA, no PEFT, no model editing, no continual learning, no catastrophic forgetting, no distillation, no self-training. The paper never proposes feeding its artifacts back into weights — unlike Letta STC, which at least gestured at the $E\to\Theta$ composition as future work.
Theta_path.nearest_neighbour: Gao et al. 2025, 'A survey of self-evolving agents', cited once in the inference-time-compute paragraph as another reactive method.

bio_CLS_path.citations: ZERO neuroscience. No McClelland/CLS, no hippocampal replay, no sleep consolidation, no dreaming literature.
bio_CLS_path.what_replaces_it: PSYCHOLOGY. Two of the 26 references are behavioural-science papers on proactive coping — Greenglass 1999 (the Proactive Coping Inventory) and Drummond & Brough 2016 — and they are cited to license the paper's central move: 'This limitation contrasts with the psychological concept of proactive coping ... a future-oriented strategy in which individuals anticipate upcoming demands, accumulate resources, and prepare for prospective goals before those demands fully materialize.' [§1, p.1].
bio_CLS_path.finding: This is a new row for the book's biology chapter. ch23 §23.8 argues that the $E$-path adopted the sleep vocabulary without the CLS argument. ProAct declines the sleep vocabulary entirely and imports a DIFFERENT human-science warrant — one about anticipation rather than consolidation, and one that actually matches its mechanism. Where Letta STC borrowed a word it did not need, ProAct borrowed a theory it could use. That is the first case in the corpus of a cross-disciplinary citation doing load-bearing work rather than decorative work, and the book should credit it while noting that no result depends on it.

cross_path_citations.what_it_DOES_engage: Agent memory architectures, proactive/anticipatory dialogue (Liao 2023, Deng 2023, Lu 2024, De Min 2026), self-reflective agents (Reflexion, Voyager, MetaReflection), tool use (ToolACE, Wang 2025), and deployed always-on assistants named in prose without citation — 'More recent agent systems such as OpenClaw and Hermes move toward always-on personal assistants, enabling scheduled checks, reminders, and automated task execution' [§2, p.3]. The intellectual parentage it claims is HUMAN–AI INTERACTION, not memory research and not inference systems.
cross_path_citations.monograph_implication: [note-writer] Letta STC situated itself in caching and speculative decoding. ProAct situates itself in proactive dialogue and coping psychology. The two members of the Precompute column claim parentage in two different fields, neither of which is memory research, and one of them files the other under a third. The spine thesis's clause (i) — that these papers do not know each other — needs a stronger formulation for this pair: they do not merely fail to cite; they cite and misread.

systems_implications.preamble: Grounding key: [PAPER] = a number or statement on the page with a locator; [INFERENCE] = the note-writer's translation. This paper supplies more systems numbers than any other $E$-path paper in the corpus, and the chapter should say so before it says anything else.

items.claim: Nothing in the decode kernel changes and shared-weight batching is preserved. The wake request is an ordinary request whose prompt carries retrieved artifacts.
items.grounding: [INFERENCE] grounded in P8 and in the total absence of training, adapters or per-user weights. [PAPER] Table 10, p.17 — every ProActEval condition runs on the same two vendor APIs. Confirms ch29 표 29-3's first row for the $E$-path.

items.claim: SLEEP-TIME COST IS FINALLY A NUMBER: 111.8k active tokens per conversation, against 69.8k for the undirected variant and 0 for the reactive baseline, with an accounting boundary that excludes the reactive response.
items.grounding: [PAPER] Table 2, p.8; Table 10, p.17; App. E, p.15. This is the quantity ch25 and X3 have been unable to obtain from twenty-nine papers, and its definition is the cleanest in the corpus.

items.claim: Sleep cost per unit of delivered benefit is now computable, and it is large: about 93.2k active tokens per turn of completion saved, about 105.0k per user turn saved, about 31.8k per anticipated need.
items.grounding: [본서 산술] from Table 2, p.8 and Table 3, p.8. None of these ratios appears in the paper. For a fleet this is the capacity-planning number: a conversation that costs a few thousand tokens to serve reactively costs 111.8k more to serve proactively.

items.claim: TOTAL COMPUTE RISES. Wall-clock per scenario-condition goes 264.8 s → 687.2 s, a factor of 2.60, and the paper claims no compute or latency saving anywhere.
items.grounding: [PAPER] Table 10, p.17; §6, p.9. [INFERENCE] This is not offloading work from an interactive tier to a batch tier — the shape Letta STC priced at 10:1 — it is net new background load bought for a human-time metric. The two Precompute papers therefore make opposite demands on a serving fleet: one reduces interactive tokens, the other adds background tokens.

items.claim: The sleep job is batchable and preemptible, but it has serial depth. Each idle window is a chain of at least four separately prompted model calls (predict → score → search/synthesise → push-score), with up to three candidates and an incremental sub-question decomposition when store coverage is low.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §3.3–§3.4, pp.4–5; App. C, p.13; App. F, p.15. [INFERENCE] Serial depth bounds how many conversations a fleet can pre-warm per unit time, exactly as Letta STC's $J\le10$ rewrite chain does. Neither paper reports the realised chain length or any throughput figure.

items.claim: The wake-time prefill delta is bounded by a retriever rather than by the whole store — a structural improvement over Letta STC, whose $\mathrm{ret}$ is the identity — but the prompt length is still never reported.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §3.4, p.5 and App. J, p.17 establish vector and temporal retrieval. [INFERENCE] Selective retrieval caps the prefill growth that `letta-stc` flags as 'the single largest systems gap in the work'. ProAct closes the mechanism half of that gap and leaves the measurement half exactly where it was: no $|\hat c|$, no prompt token count, no prefill accounting.

items.claim: THE CORPUS'S FIRST WAKE-SIDE RETRIEVAL LATENCY: about 40 ms per read and 60 ms per write for ProAct, in a table that also prices seven baselines — including MemGPT at 1.042 s per read and MemoryBank at 15.705 s per write.
items.grounding: [PAPER] Table 16, p.22. [INFERENCE] At ~40 ms a vector read is a real but non-dominant TTFT contributor for an interactive assistant; at 1.042 s it is the dominant one. This is the first row of a table the book has wanted since ch25, and the MemGPT figure is directly usable in ch13's boundary-case discussion. It must be quoted with its scope: this is the store operation only, not the 111.8k-token pipeline.

items.claim: Where the traffic lands: application-level vector + relational + document store → retriever → tokenizer → prefill → KV cache. Never HBM-resident weights, never optimizer state, never a per-user weight shard.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §2, p.2 for the three storage kinds; App. U, pp.24–25 for the write path. [INFERENCE] Identical to Letta STC's placement, and the sharpest contrast to draw against the $\Theta$-path in ch29 — the $E$-path's write traffic is text into a database, and only the $\Theta$-path's write traffic creates a memory-device opportunity. ProAct adds no new memory-device argument and the chapter should not manufacture one.

items.claim: AN OUTPUT-CHANNEL ADMISSION CONTROL EXISTS, AND IT IS RATE-LIMITED. 'When multiple artifacts exceed the push threshold in the same idle window, only the highest-scoring artifact is delivered immediately and the rest are retained as $d_z=\mathrm{queue}$.'
items.grounding: [PAPER] App. C, p.14. [INFERENCE] For a serving system this is a notification budget, and it is a cost the book's four symbols cannot carry because it is spent by the user, not by the machine. It is the first implementation of the term OUTLOOK O7 records as empty in both corpora.

items.claim: The 'when to sleep' controller is a five-second constant, which is where a real deployment would put a scheduler.
items.grounding: [PAPER] App. F, p.15. [INFERENCE] The paper builds admission control for WHAT and WHETHER and leaves WHEN and HOW MUCH as constants. In a fleet, WHEN is the queue policy and HOW MUCH is the budget allocator, and those are the two the paper does not build.

items.claim: The monograph reader's standing question — 'so what changes at decode?' — has the same answer as in ch14, and that is itself the finding: nothing changes at decode. What changes is that a background pipeline of known token cost runs between turns and occasionally writes a row.
items.grounding: [INFERENCE] grounded in P4, P6, P8. Three years and two papers into the Precompute column, the serving-stack delta is still zero, and the accounting delta is now one printed number.
